Chapter 10: Embracing the Ongoing Journey.
Let’s take a moment to talk about something that’s easy to forget—healing from trauma isn’t about reaching a final, perfect destination. It’s really about staying on a journey that keeps unfolding. Our bodies and minds are always shifting, adapting, and learning. Even after you’ve made real progress, life can throw new challenges your way, and old habits might sneak back in.
So, what does it really mean to embrace this ongoing journey? It calls for patience, humility, and a whole lot of self-compassion. You’ve got to let go of the idea that healing is quick, or that one day you’ll wake up and it’ll all be done. Instead, it’s about building a relationship with yourself—one that’s flexible, forgiving, and even a little curious.
Here are a few attitudes that can really support you along the way:
Gentle persistence—just keep practicing self-awareness and self-regulation, even on days when it feels like you’re moving at a snail’s pace.
Openness to change—letting new insights, experiences, and relationships shape you as you go.
And trust in your body—believing that your body really can adapt and recover, even if there are setbacks.
Think of healing like tending to a garden. There are seasons of growth and seasons of rest. Sometimes things are blooming beautifully, and other times, you need to do a little pruning. The work is never totally finished. But every small act of care you offer helps your life become more vibrant and resilient.
When you embrace the ongoing nature of healing, you naturally approach yourself—and others—with more kindness and understanding. Suddenly, it’s not just about fixing what’s broken. It’s about nurturing what’s already whole inside you.
